reviews.text: Professionalism to the Team! Ms. Benedetta is a 1000-star secretary: professional, capable, kind, and perfect.

The staff were helpful, extremely kind, and above all, knowledgeable. We arrived in the middle of the night with our little bully, who was in terrible pain with his stomach, and we were admitted to the emergency room for an examination and various tests.
Dr. Stefano Landolfi and the on-duty nurse Mariangela Schioppi were wonderful, competent, and above all meticulous with my dog, Pocho. They performed all the tests and treatments carefully and professionally.
I truly thank the facility and especially the two professionals for being so humane and affectionate with my dog ​​and with us.
It's 6am and the emergency room is closed 😡
Competent and very helpful staff.

I've already given this place a very positive review, some time ago.
But today I want to reiterate my thanks to all the hospital staff. This time, my Milu' and I thank Dr. Basile.
Even though it was a Sunday, they were prompt, kind, and professional as always.
My cat has an eye problem, and all the necessary tests were done.
Thanks again from me, and lots of kisses from Milu' 😍🥰😻❤️

We arrived at this clinic at 1:00 a.m. After calling, we explained that the dog had had a seizure, but they didn't even look at him. After waiting quite a while, other people were walking past us. We asked, but only then were they told they were full.
I absolutely do not recommend this clinic. Don't bring your pets; they are people without the slightest empathy.

I went to the emergency clinic because I found a dog that had been hit by a car. Upon arrival, the doctor and her team were quick and loving in providing prompt first aid. I thank them for their work and the humanity they showed both towards the little dog, who later learned her name was Masha, and towards us, who were heartbroken to see her in pain. Thank you ❤️
Professional, empathetic, and available 24/7! A service that should be replicated! Congratulations.

I went for a problem with my dog ​​and was greeted with a meticulous and professional welcome by Dr. Maiello and Nurse Mariangela, who guided me towards the best treatment plan.
Thank you so much ❤️, Naples, through you, offers a great service.
If your pet is dying over the weekend, stay home, there's a better chance it will survive.
A huge thank you to Dr. Larocca from Filiberto and many compliments for her expertise and professionalism.

NEGATIVE EXPERIENCE, BE CAREFUL, I WOULD REPORT THIS, DO NOT GO!!!!❌❌❌❌❌

I took my dog ​​to this clinic after an accident and was told he had a simple bladder contusion. The problem is that, later, it turned out that the problem was completely different, and that the diagnosis I had been given at this clinic did not match my dog's actual problem.
Despite the accident, an evaluation was not performed that, in my opinion, adequately took into account the spine and legs. I was also offered an abdominal ultrasound, with additional costs, while the actual problem was of a completely different nature.
Concerned because the dog continued to feel unwell, I contacted my trusted veterinarian, who immediately understood that the situation was not what I had been told at this clinic and identified the real problem, finally allowing us to intervene correctly.
The next day, I took my dog ​​back to this clinic because he was very limp and the treatment I'd been prescribed wasn't working. I expected a new visit and a thorough reassessment. Instead, I was simply told to wait and that there was nothing they could do, without the dog being re-examined as I'd expected.
I felt completely abandoned in managing a situation involving my dog's health. My experience was one of wasting time and incurring expenses without initially receiving a correct diagnosis.
I'm also thinking specifically of veterinarian Serena Cristiano, who examined my dog. Based on my personal experience, I would never entrust my pet to this facility again, and I strongly recommend seeking a second veterinary opinion if any problems arise.
This experience left me deeply disappointed and dissatisfied.

Terrible experience. I called during the night because I needed to take my eight-month-old Amstaff puppy, who had been vomiting for hours. A young man answered the phone and told me in advance that, if necessary, they couldn't admit him because they didn't have room. At this point, I explained that I needed emergency care to avoid worsening consequences and to ensure, with an examination and possible ultrasound, that he hadn't ingested a foreign body without my knowledge. He replied that they couldn't perform the ultrasound because there wasn't a sonographer available. Bottom line: they couldn't guarantee emergency care. I had the feeling that the guy who answered the phone was a rookie who wasn't capable of handling the situation he was about to face. Despite having explained the whole situation in detail, he couldn't advise me anything other than taking him elsewhere.

In short, this clinic is a fake 24-hour veterinary emergency room.

I discovered this clinic thanks to Dr. Giuliana Testa, and I'm truly happy our paths crossed.
I frequent this clinic with my dogs, and I want to sincerely thank a few people who, at different times, have truly made a difference for me.

Dr. Giuliana Testa, however, holds a truly special place in me. She is someone I respect and deeply fond of. She is always present, always available, and impeccable in everything she does. Even when she's not physically close to me, she always manages to be there and make me feel I can count on her. She's always ready to listen to me, answer my questions, and help me, even from afar.
She cares for my dogs with a kindness, attention, and professionalism that mean the world to me, but what I appreciate even more is the way she cares for me, too. She understands my anxieties and worries and always knows how to reassure me, find the right words, and make me feel less alone in the most difficult moments. For me, she's more than just someone to whom I entrust my dogs: she's a true guarantee, an important presence, and someone I trust completely. I wouldn't trade her for anyone. ❤️

A heartfelt thank you also to Sara Cucciniello and Silvia Contaldo, who assisted me during a nighttime emergency with great professionalism, helpfulness, and above all, a great sense of humanity. In such difficult times, finding people who are present and reassuring really makes a difference.

And a special thank you to Roberta Pasquariello, who treated my Rhodesian Ridgeback for a fracture. She performed the X-rays with great professionalism and patience, explaining everything clearly and carefully answering all my questions. For me, this too means caring not only for the animal, but also for the person who cares for it.

I'm truly grateful to have met people like this. Expertise is important, but when it's accompanied by helpfulness, patience, kindness, and humanity, you really feel the difference. And for me, Giuliana represents just that. Thank you so much to all of you for taking such good care of my dogs and, in so many ways, of me too. ❤️
Thank you Mrs. Polise, a hug to little Mia!🥰 …
Thank you Mr. Reale for your review
Wonderful staff. Great experience and kindness.

Terrible service, to say the least. Our kitten fell from the third floor chasing something and seriously injured his leg. We called the center in question and they told us to call the local health authority. We called the number provided by the operator and they told us to go to a private provider. We called back because it was urgent and we wanted to take him to a place where they could take care of him as soon as possible. The result? The operator on the phone somehow concluded that we wouldn't pay for the care... and these places should exist because of the shared love we have for animals. One star is even too much.

We first came to Vet Village last July when our beloved Bullo (a 10-year-old Jack Russell) suffered a urinary blockage due to stones. During the examination, he was also found to have a lump in his testicles that our trusted vet had never identified despite several ultrasounds and other symptoms. He underwent successful surgery the next day and was discharged after 24 hours of observation. Today, he is doing great and has regained his proverbial energy. Thanks to all the staff for their professionalism.

On the night between the 26th and 27th, I went to this emergency veterinary clinic with my dog, and unfortunately, the experience was terrible in every way.
The situation was completely chaotic: just one doctor, Maria F., and a nurse managing everything. The visit lasted less than 10 minutes, and I paid €100 just for the exam (it's not about the money; I would have paid millions to keep my dog ​​healthy).
During the attempt to perform an blood gas analysis, Dr. Maria F. was unable to obtain my dog's vein and pricked his leg three times. Eventually, the nurse had to intervene, and he was able to take the blood sample.
During the exam, a suspected heart murmur was also detected. When we returned to our trusted veterinarian, the murmur was not detected. At a time of great concern for your pet's health, being given information that is then completely contradicted by another veterinary evaluation is very perplexing, to say the least. We were also told that the dog needed an MRI. Our veterinarian, assessing the situation, advised us against it immediately, believing it could be counterproductive or pose an unnecessary risk to the dog at that time.
We were also given two IVs, told that they would help the dog recover over the next few days. The dog subsequently improved and recovered without further IVs, which made us question the actual need for those treatments.
What struck me most was the complete lack of empathy and care for both the animal and the owner. In an emergency situation, one is already terrified about their dog's condition and would expect professionalism, organization, clarity, and above all, humanity.
Unfortunately, my impression was that the management was much more concerned with costs than with the actual need for the services. €100 for a visit lasting less than 10 minutes, additional services and treatments, and, most importantly, recommendations that were later questioned by our veterinarian: all of this left us truly disappointed.
Finally, the report hadn't even been uploaded: if I hadn't called personally to request it, I don't know when I would have received it.
In a veterinary emergency room, especially when you arrive terrified for your pet's health, you expect to find professionalism, expertise, organization, and empathy.
Unfortunately, my experience with Dr. Maria F. and this facility was exactly the opposite.
I absolutely cannot recommend this emergency room.

I'll respond to your response by clarifying a few things.

During the stay in the IV room, I was completely alone with my dog. The doctor never came in; only the nurse came in twice to change the bag (1 minute each) and a third time because the dog had disconnected the IV. On that occasion, I had to open the door and raise my voice to be heard. If necessary, you can check on the cameras.

My veterinarian has been treating my dog ​​for 13 years and is a professional with an intimate knowledge of his medical history.

During our stay, I also witnessed complaints from several other owners. I believe this should be a starting point for reflection and improvement.

Reviews are designed to highlight what went wrong and allow the facility to learn from its mistakes, as well as to warn other owners. Responding by trying to justify every criticism, rather than listening to it, doesn't seem like the best way to improve the service.

My review simply recounts my experience, and for this reason, I stand by what I've already written: I don't recommend this facility.

I found Noel on December 8th, four years ago, in the rain, abandoned. I entrusted him to the care of Dr. Antonella Vitiello. Everything seemed fine until a few months later, during a checkup, she realized something was wrong. The diagnosis shocked us both. He had pericardial effusion. I didn't even know what it was. The following months were hell. She had to extract fluid from his pericardium seven times. We went urgently, day and night, whenever Noel's abdomen swelled. She was always there, along with other doctors. I remember Dr. Gabriele's professionalism and Alessandra's kindness, reassuring me and Noel every time Dr. Vitiello tried to save his life. Seven times before his heart surgery. It seemed the storm had passed, and Noel was entrusted to the excellent care of cardiologist Dr. Molinaro. We did everything possible, even the impossible, to give him a life, and it lasted three and a half years. Unfortunately, Noel passed away this summer. I want to thank everyone, the entire clinic staff, but especially Dr. Vitiello, because without her, Noel wouldn't have lived a single day. Her professionalism, but also her great humanity and the will to fight together, helped give my kitten these three and a half years of life, so he could enjoy all the love we were able to give him.

Dr. Maiello was exceptional; he saved our colony's kitten in a minute, and along with Nurse Liguori, they are all incredibly kind and knowledgeable. I found empathy, true love for animals, and a great deal of professionalism. I recommend VetVillage to everyone! The best 🩷🧡💛💚

Absolutely never bring your loves here... they have no love for them at all nor empathy for their owners... they only think about how much money they should receive to always have them do the same useless tests... they killed our love (not directly mine but that I raised together with my friend) who had gastric cancer... they "followed" him for more than two months only with ultrasounds and IVs without further investigation and postponing specific visits and tests... rightly it was August... They just wanted to hospitalize him... shame that whoever had said so went on vacation the next day... He would have remained there alone and abandoned... luckily we moved on... and then fortunately we met an angel of an oncologist from another clinic who with boundless love and care accompanied him until the end... but... We arrived late... because he was treated and looked after poorly and with great, great neglect... Always ask for other opinions because you might be lucky enough to meet competent and loving doctors like we did...

I'm giving one star because it's the minimum; if I could, I'd give it zero. I went for an EMERGENCY for my dying cat. They opened the door, made me wait, and then rudely told me they were closed. They didn't even give the cat a glance. Terrible.

I'll tell you about my experience: my dog ​​arrived at the emergency room dying with pancreatitis and ongoing sepsis. The promptness and professionalism of the clinic's medical staff are indescribable! I will never forget the love with which they cared for him and the attention with which they cared for and cared for him. Thank you with all my heart for allowing Drago to come home, and thank you to all the doctors and nurses for the professionalism and love you have given us.

Thank you
Carmen and Drago
Thank you very much for your review!
Thanks Vera for your review! 💛 …

On September 28, 2026, they recommended this veterinary clinic to us. It's been a worse choice.
We waited three hours as soon as we entered, then finally a pseudo-doctor emerged from somewhere who knew little. As soon as we entered with the kitten, she immediately gave us an examination, without even delving into the cause.
After taking her temperature, she immediately painted a grim picture, lacking empathy for either the owners or the kitten.
That said, after asking some trivial questions, she immediately talked about hospitalization estimates and much more, without even, in my opinion, having examined her properly, given her many animals.
That said, she doesn't recommend it to anyone; it's just like a discount store where they're trying to get as much money out of you as possible.
Thank you, Mr. Travaglione, for your review. 😀 …
Thank you, Mr. D'Amore, for the kind review. A hug to Cioco!

I went to this facility for my dog's hemorrhagic ear infection. After a two-and-a-half-hour wait, they admitted me. A veterinarian asked a colleague to proceed with the examination but was told she couldn't because she was already busy compiling reports. They told me to leave and wait a little longer. When I asked how long, they told me they couldn't tell me, but that it could be a dermatological issue, not serious, so I could come back the next day to schedule an appointment with the dermatologist. I'm deeply sorry for the superficiality, lack of attention, and lack of empathy shown, and I hope I never find myself in an emergency situation again. Tomorrow morning, I'll contact my trusted veterinarian.

The only facility with 24-hour inpatient care in Naples. They work incredibly hard and are meticulous. We hope my dog ​​gets better soon. She received the care and attention she deserves.
Pay attention to the reports; they always lack information (for example, the medication administered).
Being the only emergency location, they are overcrowded.
The ultrasound doctor never provides information, and you have to wait several days for the report; she's a bit snobbish.
The only major flaw is the costs, which are truly above average.

The oncologist is an excellent, competent, and helpful professional, to whom we extend our deepest gratitude. Thanks to the treatment she prescribed, which was well tolerated and compatible with a good quality of life, our dog lived approximately five months, compared to the average survival rate of approximately three months that had been predicted. Therefore, our assessment of her work is absolutely positive.

Unfortunately, the same cannot be said for the entire experience we had at the facility, especially during the final hours of our 14-year-old dog's life, who was suffering from terminal cancer.

It is important to clarify that neither the severity of the clinical situation nor the final decision, of which the family was fully aware, are being questioned. Precisely because it was a definitive and painful decision, certain certainties and, above all, clear and comprehensive technical answers were needed before proceeding.

When asked specific questions about the tests performed and not performed, and in particular the request to understand why a complete blood count had not been performed in the presence of a bloody thoracic effusion, the matter was essentially dismissed as "nonsense," presumably because it was deemed unnecessary given the animal's terminal condition. The point, however, was not to determine whether that test would alter the prognosis or the final decision, but to obtain a technical explanation and a thorough understanding of the clinical picture before making an irreversible decision.

When it was pointed out that, despite his clinical condition, the dog was still standing, the response received was: "I'm standing too." A frankly inappropriate, rude, and completely lacking the sensitivity one would expect at such a moment.

Before euthanasia, the dog was also politely asked to review the ultrasound image of the newly discovered effusion, not to challenge the clinical assessment, but simply to have further objective evidence before making an irreversible decision. It was reported that the image had not been saved and that only the one relating to the examination performed three days earlier was available.

Even the subsequent technical questions were not provided with sufficiently clear and comprehensive explanations.

There was no attempt to replace the veterinarians, nor to deny the evidence of a terminal illness: the request was simply to understand the clinical data and the reasons for the assessments performed. These questions were asked, moreover, by people perfectly capable of understanding medical-scientific explanations.

What made the experience even more disconcerting was what happened immediately after the euthanasia. We were asked, "The dog weighed 26 kg, correct?" When we replied that it actually weighed 19.9 kg, we were essentially told that it appeared to weigh more and that a dose based on 36 kg had been calculated/administered. I report this episode without going into the pharmacological appropriateness of the dose used, which is not the point of this review.

What is most disappointing, therefore, is not the clinical conclusion, but the way in which completely legitimate requests were met: hasty responses, superficiality, disrespectful tones, and a clear lack of empathy during one of the most difficult times for pet lovers.

Technical expertise is certainly essential, but it should always be accompanied by professional communication, a willingness to provide explanations, respect, and empathy. This is even more true when a family is about to say goodbye to a pet who has been a part of their lives for fourteen years.

Based on my overall experience, and despite my excellent rating of the oncologist and my deep gratitude, I strongly advise against this clinic.
They are terrible, don't go there if you love your pet.
I wanted to congratulate this facility and in particular Dr. Serena for how she welcomed us and our little girl, they really saved her life. I highly recommend this facility to anyone who needs it.

Hello Ms. Maria Francesca,
Thank you for leaving your review. We'd love to learn how we can improve based on your experience. If you'd like, you can call us or email us. Your opinion is important to us.
They are worth 0, they never answer the phone, stay away from them

I'm leaving this review because I was looking for one before my dog ​​had a dental cleaning with sedation.
I own a Toy Pincher (a small breed prone to dental tartar). Unfortunately, my dog ​​won't let me brush her teeth at all. I've tried everything, and after several years, her teeth/gums/mouth condition unfortunately required a proper cleaning. I've always been super scared of having her undergo a dental cleaning solely because of the general anesthesia she'd have to endure. I was very happy at Vet Village; my dog ​​was super healthy as soon as she woke up and perfectly herself! Before the procedure, she underwent tests and check-ups, which gave me greater peace of mind! Thanks so much to the vet doctors, Mya now has a healthy mouth and decent breath 😂❤️

I sincerely thank Vet Village for their care for our cat with urinary blockage. It was the only facility open Saturday night between the provinces of Naples and Caserta, which is why so many emergencies flocked there. Without their timely intervention, our Sirio would not have made it.
The doctor and nurse on duty worked tirelessly, but were clearly overwhelmed by the emergencies. It's unacceptable that such a large area doesn't have other emergency rooms open at night and on weekends; we need more facilities and more staff. A huge thank you to the staff for what they do.

The staff were helpful, and I was finally admitted to the emergency room for my cat, but I had to wait over four hours for the 8:30 PM changeover, as there were already appointments booked.
More precise communication from the receptionist would have been helpful: when I called in the morning, I wasn't told I needed to book an appointment for the afternoon. This would have saved me a long wait.
Furthermore, it would be very helpful to have a bathroom available for patients waiting in the waiting room.
Dr. Schinaia was wonderful with my Lucky: he carefully and cleanly aspirated the pus from an abscess, without anesthesia, because my cat is very well behaved. I'm very happy with the doctor's care. I'm truly happy that he examined my cat so carefully. I always thank the facility for being welcoming and very humane.

One of the best veterinary clinics in Naples. They are all truly professional; if you need to entrust your furry friend to them, definitely bring him here. My Scarlett was treated with immense love and passion by Dr. Filazzola, a truly excellent doctor who, with her professionalism, got my Whippet back on track. I'm truly grateful to her!! Thank you, Dr. Maria, and hugs from Scarlett!
Thanks for the 5 💫 …

I was yesterday with my eight year old Maltese Gabriel, on Saturday evening, in the emergency room because the day before I had been to my local vet with a urinary blockage. They were very good and professional, they did all the necessary checks and reassured me that the dog was better the next day and the worry was gone.

I brought my cat in at night because of a burst abscess. Upon arrival, they made us wait quite a while, but fortunately, it wasn't a problem since my cat wasn't in critical condition. The on-site doctor (whose name I won't reveal because this comment is intended to help others and isn't intended to be defamatory) gave him a general check-up; she then shaved the area where the hole from the burst abscess had appeared. She disinfected it with specific medications, but didn't apply a bandage. They left him with the hole open. The next day, we immediately took him to our trusted vet, who, fortunately, thoroughly disinfected him and applied a bandage. For the general check-up, which didn't require any special equipment except a thermometer and a razor (if they can be considered such), they charged €100. They then charged another €60 if we wanted to follow up with a complete blood count, but we preferred to have it done by our vet. I appreciated the care and concern shown, but it seemed extremely superficial compared to that of other vets, especially ours, who unfortunately wasn't there that night. Furthermore, I understand that it was a nighttime procedure, but the cost is extremely excessive compared to the treatment. In addition, they made us create a profile—absolutely unnecessary—and sign a privacy policy without asking us to read it first or explain what it was about, but the nurse checked all the boxes in the document on her own initiative. At the time, I let it go, but later I asked myself two questions. I can't stand organizations that deal with mental and physical health and treat clients like numbers. Absolutely not recommended for us; unfortunately, it was an emergency.
Thank you! 🤩 …
I brought one of my stray kittens and found the staff kind and helpful and Dr. Vitiello very good and empathetic.

I've been going to VetVillage for years.
A special shout-out goes to Dr. Vitiello and Dr. Gentile, who have become my go-tos: excellent professionals, always available, and so human.
A money-making machine, with no responsible veterinarian. Outside veterinarians are called in at random when needed, often with disastrous results. Highly discouraged.
Successful, life-saving thoracentesis completed stress-free for a cat with heart disease.
Never going back, zero empathy, I had a bad feeling.

Run away. Only money, easy tears, can't make it, they say, but there's no cure... Run away from this place... we'll call you even during the night... If there are complications... Then they'll call you the next day at 7am! ​​Visiting hours tell you he's DEAD... Why don't you call during the night? God will see to it, He'll provide.
Thank you so much! 🤩 …

An experience to forget. My two-month-old baby is sick. I arrived at the facility, but they didn't accept me and sent me away without even examining him.
Even though I said he hadn't eaten or drunk for a day, if I could give him zero stars, I would have done so already.

The facility was spotlessly clean and immediately ready to assist. I arrived with my dog, who had suffered heat stroke. He was immediately assisted and given excellent care. The doctor was very kind and helpful.
I brought my dog ​​in with huge testicles. They couldn't tell what it was, so they gave him a syringe and sent him home. It was a tumor.
Excellent veterinary facility in Naples
After a long wait they gave us the prognosis... Kind and helpful staff!
Thank you for saving my Alex with professionalism, care, and empathy: the perfect team! A special thanks to Enrica for the love she puts into her work! Eternally grateful!
Extraordinary animal care facility.

I went on a Saturday for a feline emergency. We were greeted with professionalism and kindness. Despite several emergency rooms at the same time, the entire staff, from the doctors to the reception, showed care for each individual, providing directions, thorough explanations, and prompt treatment.

Negative experience, they made us go and come back 3/4 times without even telling us what the dog has. They gave us an appointment for a gastroscopy because the dog was vomiting blood. I called 2 days before the visit and apparently there was no appointment and they don't know when the doctor who can perform it will be there. They don't even know how to communicate with each other. A completely negative experience, zero professionalism.

I've been attending Vet Village for several years now, and my experience has always been very positive. I'm particularly cared for by gastroenterologist Serena Cristiano, whom I consider to be a truly expert professional. She's competent, meticulous, and always available to clearly explain every aspect of the diagnostic and treatment process. I've found a team that's competent, helpful, and attentive to both animals and their owners. I particularly appreciate the staff's kindness and willingness to answer questions and concerns. This facility inspires trust and care for animal welfare. Highly recommended.

Hello Ms. Ronchi,
We can't find any folders associated with your name, so we can't explain the 3 stars. We'd appreciate it if you could contact us to help us understand what you think we can improve.
Thank you.
Thanks for the 5 ⭐

This morning I took my 17-year-old dachshund to this clinic because, due to his age, he doesn't always feel the urge to urinate, so every now and then he needs to have a bladder pressure maneuver performed. The clinic was exceptionally closed for reasons I don't know; however, the person who came to open the gate for a couple whose dog had sadly died agreed to have a doctor perform the maneuver despite the closure. What can I say? Thank you for your kindness and empathy.

I would like to extend my heartfelt thanks to Drs. Sara and Giuliana, who accompanied Jack with great kindness and dignity on his final journey, to the sonographer Gabriele, and to all the nurses and receptionists at Vet Village for their professionalism, expertise, and, above all, the humanity they demonstrated during an extremely difficult journey. In such delicate moments, sensitivity and care for the patient and his family truly make a difference, and they demonstrated this at every opportunity.

Unfortunately, I cannot express the same opinion regarding the oncology management. I encountered significant difficulties communicating with the oncologist, who was available exclusively via email and often had response times that were incompatible with the sensitive and urgent nature of cancer patients. Furthermore, the responses were frequently incomplete, forcing me to send additional emails to obtain clarification on dosages, methods, and timing of the therapies.

A particularly critical episode occurred when Jack developed epididymitis and I urgently needed to know whether it was appropriate to supplement his therapy with an antibiotic. I only received a response after about 24 hours, and even then, it wasn't conclusive. In the meantime, I had to contact my trusted veterinarian to arrange the necessary treatment and report the situation to the clinic.

Another episode that left me very perplexed concerns a chemotherapy session scheduled for 11:00 a.m. Due to unforeseen work-related issues, I notified the clinic around 11:30 a.m. that I would be late and showed up around 1:00 p.m., apologizing for the inconvenience. Despite explaining the difficulties in balancing work commitments with such a demanding treatment program, and despite the fact that the day was dedicated to chemotherapy, no alternative solution was considered to still carry out the treatment. The session was postponed to the following week. While I understand the need to respect the facility's organization, I would have expected greater availability and attention to the needs of an oncology patient.

I understand that specialist work is complex and demanding, but I believe that in the oncology field, availability, timeliness, communication, and patient care are fundamental. For this reason, although I had a very positive experience with most of the Vet Village staff, I would not recommend the facility for the management of oncology cases.
I found people of great humanity, competent and kind.
Mrs. Hauber, thanks for the 5 ⭐! A kiss to little Tommy 🥰 …
Excellent facility with very empathetic and professional doctors and nurses. They were top notch during the emergency.

I'd really like to know why they're not answering. I'm honestly trying to call because I have an urgent situation, but no one is bothering to answer.

I'd also like to add that, as per the website, you have about 3 numbers. Don't answer any of them soon. Don't text me if it's urgent. Call this number so we can find the right person for you when you come. That's not the case. I've been calling for about an hour and no one has bothered to read or answer. It's about my pet. Don't call yourself a 24-hour clinic, etc., or don't put an emergency number. If you don't answer the phone, it makes no sense.
Highly recommended...
Positive experience with Dr. Cristiano Serena, very professional, she immediately solved my little Leo's problem, I recommend her

A lifesaving experience! Guardian angels for our four-legged friends
I couldn't be more grateful to VetVillage! On Sunday evening, I was in a panic over an emergency with my kitten. With no experience whatsoever, I found an extraordinary team.
Dr. Testa, Dr. Vitiello, Dr. Maiello, and technician Enrica Sepe helped the little one with unparalleled skill and kindness, showering him with cuddles. A special thanks to Annabella Zullo, who handles the administrative side impeccably.
The kitten was hospitalized for two days: they kept me constantly updated, providing me with immense human support. Thank you so much for saving my kitten and for being so close to me during a very scary time!
If you find yourself in an emergency—or even for routine visits—trust them with your eyes closed.

I can only highly recommend the clinic. It's truly rare to find a place where professional expertise and profound empathy blend like this.
The reception staff is always friendly, but the real strength, however, is the medical team. I entrusted my dog ​​Oscar to them and was impressed by the thoroughness of the examination and the clarity of the explanations. Dr. Testa demonstrated not only impeccable clinical preparation, but also infinite kindness and patience, putting my pet completely at ease. A special thanks also to Dr. Maiello.
VERY BAD SERVICE, RUDENESS, LACK OF RESPECT AND POOR PROFESSIONALISM

At the Vet Village, from December 31st to March 6th, I lived alongside my Remo a journey of fear, hope, and love. We were there almost every day, for the treatments that Remo would have refused without me.
And in that suspended time, I found something you don't often encounter: real people.
They welcomed our daily presence in the waiting room for treatment without ever making me feel inconvenienced; on the contrary, they supported me, comforted me, and made me feel less alone. Doctors, nurses, and the receptionist Benedetta supported me, understood me, embraced me even without words.
Remo was never "just a patient." He was looked at, touched, called by name... loved.
A huge thank you to Dr. Conforti, his doctor, capable of combining exceptional expertise and sensitivity, explaining, reassuring, supporting... He wasn't just a doctor. He was a guide, a strong yet profoundly human presence. I will never forget his shining eyes, his sincere compassion in the most difficult moment. In that moment, I realized that Remo was truly in loving hands.
Dr. Vitiello fought for him with a determination that can't be explained, only admired. She never stopped searching, trying, hoping.
The sweet Dr. Testa called him "a special dog"... and truly made him feel that way.
And with them, the nurses: Enrica, Ciccio, Francesca... and all the others whose names, unfortunately, I don't know.
Gentle hands, sweet voices, constant attention.
Unfortunately, it didn't go as we hoped, but I know for certain that nothing was left to chance. You did everything possible, with dedication, conscience, and heart.
Remo was loved. And that, to me, means more than anything.
Thank you Vet Village, because you didn't just treat: you gave your heart, your presence, your humanity.
I will never forget him. ❤️

Good evening
I apologize for disturbing you, because I know you're busy and very professional.
Could I ask how my four-legged friend IAGO is doing and what he's doing?
Thank you. Good evening.

It's been exactly three weeks since my dog ​​Maya died. I had to wait because I was too shaken by the sudden loss. Unfortunately, despite a major operation and hospital stay, she didn't make it, especially since she was elderly. I have nothing to say about the doctors and paramedics, who dedicated themselves to saving her. But the outcome was the worst ever. Even though they knew Maya was dying, they didn't give us a chance to say goodbye. For three days, we went during visiting hours, but, in agreement with the staff, we didn't go in so as not to upset her. On the last night, her condition worsened. I called at 7:00 a.m., respecting, as always, the phone office hours, and was told not to come, that they would call me. We went immediately anyway, and as soon as we crossed the threshold of the clinic, I received the phone call I never wanted to receive. Sometimes we need to understand that the bond between humans and animals is so profound that a missed opportunity leaves a lasting legacy and regrets we'll carry with us forever. Especially if the children are the ones paying the price. In my case, my children, who lack the tools to rationalize and will take a long time to overcome the guilt of not having seen her again after she entered the clinic.
I therefore want to urge you, in the future, to pay close attention to the emotional management of your patients' owners, who must be treated with great empathy, because what is effectively a bereavement, in doing so, can become damaging.
You are the best, thank you for everything, I'm happy to have met you.
Thank you!

I can only leave a very positive review for the Vet Village Veterinary Center!

Their expertise and professionalism are truly top-notch: every visit is handled with great preparation, attention to detail, and clear explanations. But what really makes the difference is the humanity and passion that are evident at every step.

Every time I bring my three cats, I feel completely at ease, knowing I'm entrusting them to expert and caring hands, who treat them with care, respect, and so much love.

A special thanks goes to Dr. Cristiano, always thorough, competent, and reassuring, and to Enrica, incredibly sweet, professional, and attentive at all times.

Thank you so much for everything you do every day: you are a precious resource for those who, like me, consider their pets part of the family ❤️🐾
We were there for a malnourished kitten, just a few days old, who was on the verge of death. Thanks to the immediate intervention of the two vets, he recovered. Thank you so much.

We were treated at Vet Village for a few years because it was close to home, following the closure of our regular clinic.
Aside from the facility's terrible disorganization, whereby we had to wait at least an hour for every scheduled checkup, my dog ​​was seen by several vets, and we never received a unanimous opinion; they always disagreed.
We recently changed vets and discovered that she was likely treated poorly, worsening her condition.
Stay away if you have any alternatives.

I would add, months later and in response to the clinic's reply, that I was indeed a client of the clinic and have the emails with the invoices to prove it. My dog ​​was simply registered in my father's name, and I'm sure a more thorough search would have revealed it.

The worst place to take your pet. Aside from the incompetence of the vets, they're completely lacking in humanity. The facility profits off your anxiety and pain by charging outrageous prices for simple tests and always suggesting a day hospital at the facility. I've had bad experiences in the past; I returned years later for an emergency, as it was unfortunately the only veterinary emergency room in the area. I had a terrible experience, and I won't go back; I'd rather move miles away.
Highly not recommended.
A little pat for little Gollum!

I would like to express my deepest gratitude to all the staff for the professionalism and humanity shown towards my little Pepe, who sadly passed away three months ago due to a complicated renal syndrome (Fanconi). Dr. Antonella Vitiello dedicated countless hours and months to ensuring the best care possible, making his final journey as peaceful as possible, also providing us with great moral support. I also entrusted her with Willy, his brother, for pancreatitis, which she successfully overcame thanks to her tenacity and dedication. Now, more than just the doctor of my little ones, she has become a great friend. Thanks also for his expertise to Dr. Stefano Landolfi, who touched me so much by dedicating one of his adopted trees to Pepe, for whom he conducted a study on Fanconi Syndrome. Heartfelt thanks to Patrizia, Willy, and Sofia, the new arrival.

These guys are extremely knowledgeable, kind, professional, and caring. Even though I'm not from Naples, they made me feel at home and didn't rip me off with ridiculous prices like 98% of vets unfortunately do.
I will be forever grateful.

Terrible experience.
We went for an ultrasound and an oncology consultation. The oncologist never contacted us, and we only received the ultrasound report after three days and numerous calls. Fortunately, we found answers and solutions by consulting another veterinary clinic.

On January 31st, I brought my dog ​​to the clinic in serious condition.
She was diagnosed with an autoimmune disease, Addison's.
I thank all the staff who managed to save her. A special thanks to Dr. Serena Cristiano.
Who explained to me how to manage the disease step by step.
Now she's finally home. She's back to eating, playing, and so on.
With the right care, attention, and regular checkups, I know I can count on this clinic.
Thank you to all the staff.

We brought my little Ulisse to the hospital in a life-threatening condition. You cared for him, cuddled him, in short, you tried to do the impossible, but unfortunately, suddenly, he no longer responded to treatment and the situation worsened.
I wanted to thank all the doctors and nurses who welcomed both us and my little one with so much love. Thank you for your empathy and great professionalism.
Thank you to Dr. Rita De Falco, Dr. Testa, Dr. Bocchetti; in short, a huge thank you to all—all of you.
However, I must extend a special thanks to Dr. Serena Cristiano because it is thanks to her remarkable sensitivity that my little one was able to enjoy his home and the company of his loved ones before leaving us forever.
Thank you from the bottom of my heart!!!
Simona Nevola and Ulisse

Efficiency, competence, availability, and, last but not least, a big heart. I desperately rushed to the emergency room in the middle of the night with my dog, who was already dying. In less than an hour, all the tests were completed, he underwent emergency surgery, and was treated with love and professionalism. After two days of hospitalization, he is here at home with me, and I deeply feel the need to thank the entire facility, especially Dr. Maria and Dr. Pasquariello.
With immense joy, I thank you!
The entire staff immediately took care of my little dog at dawn on Sunday morning. Very, very professional, meticulous, and humane. Highly recommended.

If you're looking for a place where rudeness reigns supreme and your pet's health is treated with disarming superficiality, you've come to the right place. I brought my dog ​​to this clinic hoping for medical help, but I was met with a wall of arrogance and disorganization.
After an endless and unjustified wait, the icing on the cake: nothing. I wasn't given a diagnosis, I wasn't told what was wrong with my little girl, nor was I given clear direction on how to proceed. Leaving a veterinary clinic without answers, after being treated rudely and dismissively, is simply shameful.
A doctor shouldn't just know how to treat (which wasn't the case here), but also how to communicate with owners, who arrive already full of anxiety. Instead, I found a cold environment and staff who would be better off changing careers if they don't have the patience or empathy needed to manage the public.
Save time, money, and most importantly, your pets' health: go elsewhere."

On December 30, 2025, I brought my poodle Zoey, who was in serious condition with diabetic ketoacidosis. She was immediately admitted to the hospital, and thanks to the staff's expertise, love for animals, and empathy, we managed to save her. She's now at home, but she's being monitored remotely by doctors to best manage her diabetes. Regardless of how things turn out, Vet Village is the best veterinary clinic.
